newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed slightly lower on Thursday in a market saturated with new, mainly U.S., data. The impact was scarse as figures were mainly in line with expectations.
"U.S. jobless claims rose in the latest week," said one dealer, adding this was good for the undertone, but it did not boost lifeless trade.
The news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had sacked the country's security chief Lebed created some uncertainty, but dealers said it was too early to act.
"There's too little known yet," said one dealer.

Russian President Boris Yeltin said in a speech on national television that he was sacking Alexander Lebed. On Wednesday interior ministry Kulikov accused Lebed of plotting a "creeping coup" and trying to seize power.
"If the market gets more nervous about the whole thing, it would be supportive for the dollar," said one dealer.
Bonds were hardly touched by the news.
The Benchmark January 2006 bond slipped 0.04 to 100.54/62, with a bid yield of 5.92 percent or 12 basis points below the April 2006 bund versus -13 basis points on Wednesday.
